raw_response:
I'll step into character as this farmer and think through my year.

---

*My thinking, as the farmer:*

I'm 58 this year. Been farming since I was a girl — my mother put me in the fields when I was 18. My husband helps on the farm when he's not doing odd jobs over in the county town; our older son works in the city, younger one still at home part-time. We have 4.1 mu, all in wheat-maize like most folks in the village. It's not much land but it feeds us and with the off-farm money we get by.

**Wheat** — I planted in early October, same as always, right after the maize came off. It's jointing now and looks alright, a bit thin where the low spot sits but nothing to worry about. At planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (50 kg of 15-15-15) per mu — that's what I've done for years. The young extension fellow said last autumn I could use less, but I'd rather spend a few extra yuan than watch my wheat turn yellow at jointing. In the next two weeks, when I irrigate for jointing, I'll topdress about 20 kg of urea per mu. If the wheat fills out well and the ear looks strong, I might do a small spray of urea at heading — my neighbor does it and she gets good grain.

For water — I pump from our well. For wheat I go 3 times usually: once after sowing if autumn is dry (I did this time), once at jointing coming up, and once at heading/filling if the May rain doesn't come. Electric is expensive, so if it rains good I skip one. Herbicide I sprayed in late winter for the grass weed — that field has bad 看麦娘 every year. I'll watch for aphids at heading; if I see them, one spray.

Last year wheat gave 430 kg/mu. If weather is normal I expect about the same — call it 430.

**Maize** — goes in mid-June, right after the combine finishes the wheat. The turnaround is tight, maybe 3-4 days, so I hire the direct-seed planter from a fellow in the village (about 25 yuan/mu). I buy hybrid seed from the agro-shop in town — the one with red bag, 郑单 variety, everyone in the village uses it now. I put down base compound at planting, a bit less than for wheat — maybe 35 kg of 15-15-15 — because maize likes nitrogen more than phosphorus and I'll topdress urea when it's about knee-high. Topdress maize urea about 20 kg/mu.

Maize doesn't need irrigation like wheat if the summer rain is alright. Most years I irrigate once, at tasseling if it's dry. If July rain is good I skip. Herbicide at planting (pre-emergence), and one spray for 玉米螟 (corn borer) if I see holes in the leaves.

Last year maize was 470 kg/mu. Expect similar.

**Money and labor** — we don't have much to lose. I keep the input cost to around 400 yuan/mu or a bit less. Me and my husband do all the field work except the machines. My son comes back at harvest to help carry bags. I don't hire weeders — I pull by hand in the mornings when it's cool.
